entities.summary:
Cosmas of Maiuma, also known as Cosmas Hagiopolites, Cosmas of Jerusalem, Cosmas the Melodist, or Cosmas the Poet, was a bishop and a renowned hymnographer of the 8th century. He was born in unknown circumstances and died on November 13, 760 CE. Cosmas of Maiuma was a key figure in the East, serving as bishop and contributing significantly to the development of Eastern Orthodox and Catholic hymnography. He is venerated as a saint by both churches and is considered one of the most important figures in the history of Christian worship music.

Cosmas of Maiuma was born in the late 7th century, likely in the Eastern Mediterranean region. He rose to prominence as a bishop and hymnographer, and his contributions to the development of Eastern Orthodox and Catholic worship music are still celebrated today. His most famous works include the 'Hexaemeron' and the 'Cosmas Hymn', which are still performed and studied by scholars and musicians around the world.

Cosmas of Maiuma's legacy extends beyond his contributions to worship music. He played a significant role in shaping the spiritual and cultural landscape of the Eastern Mediterranean during the 8th century. His work had a lasting impact on the development of Eastern Orthodox and Catholic theology, and his influence can still be felt in the liturgy and worship practices of these churches today.

Despite the passing of centuries, Cosmas of Maiuma's work continues to inspire and educate people around the world. His hymns and poetry are still widely studied and performed, and his legacy serves as a reminder of the enduring power of Christian worship music to bring people together and transcend cultural boundaries.
